questions.question: ‘Jat-Jatin’, ‘Jhijhian Dance’ are popular folk dances of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Bihar__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jat-Jattin:**

 
 
• It is the most popular folk dance of North Bihar, especially in Mithila and Koshi region.
 
• Jat-Jattin is the dance of women and is supposed to be performed on moonlit nights during the monsoons.
 
• Grown-up girls and young housewives gather in the courtyard and, accompanied by a drum, dance from midnight to sunrise.
 
• Men goes to far-off places to earn livelihood.
 
• Jat-Jattin is a folk dance of the same emigrant husband accompanied by his spouse.
 
• Apart from poverty and sorrow, this dance reflects a rainbow of the sweet and tender quarrel as well as some complaints between husband and wife.
 
• The folk dance mocks to comfort the hurdles of life with a smile.
 
• Through this dance, various other socially concerned topics like poverty, sorrow, love, arguments between lovers or husband and wife are also enacted.
 
• In some versions, the performers wear masks to add a real picture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Following are some famous folks dance in Bihar:-

 
 
• Jhijhian Dance
 
• Kajari Dance
 
• Sohar- Khilouna Dance
 
• Holi Dance
 
• Jhumri Dance
 
• Launda Dance

questions.question: Sattriya classical dance belongs to which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sattriya:

 
 
• Sattriya is a classical dance form of Assam in Northeast India.
 
• It was introduced in the 15th century AD by the great Vaishnava saint and reformer of Assam, Mahapurusha Sankaradeva.
 
• It was traditionally performed by male monks (bhokots) in monasteries (Sattras) as part of their daily rituals.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognized Sattriya as a classical dance in 2000.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: ‘Mohiniyattam’, is a traditional dance which originated in the state of ______ in India.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **__Kerala__.**

__
 
• **Mohiniyattam** literally interpreted as the dance of ‘Mohini’, the celestial enchantress of Hindu mythology, is the classical solo dance form of **Kerala.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• References to Mohiniyattam can be found in the texts** Vyavaharamala** written in 1709 by **Mazhamagalam Narayanan Namputiri** and in **Ghoshayatra**, written later by poet **Kunjan Nambiar**.
 
• It has elements of Bharatanatyam (grace & elegance) and Kathakali (vigor) but is more erotic, lyrical, and delicate.
 
• Mohiniyattam is characterized by graceful, swaying body movements with no abrupt jerks or sudden leaps.
 
• It belongs to the** lasya style **which is feminine, tender, and graceful.
 
• The movements are emphasized by the glides and the up and down movement on toes, like the waves of the sea and the swaying of the coconut, palm trees, and paddy fields.
 
• Realistic make-up and simple dressing (in Kasavu saree of Kerala) are used.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms depicts the anguish of women whose partners are gone from home?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biraha**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Biraha dance **and its offshoot, the Bidesia, are well-liked forms of **entertainment in rural Bihar.**
 
• It portrays the **suffering of women** whose partners have left the house.
 
• On the other side, only men who also play **female characters** can do this kind of **dancing.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Matki:**

 
 
• **The Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh**, India, is where the matki dance is most frequently practiced.
 
• Women execute this **solo dance** on special occasions.
 
 
 
• **Alkap:**
 
 
• Alkap is a traditional **village dance-drama **that is performed in the **Rajmahal Hills of Jharkhand and the Rajshahi, Murshidabad, and Malda regions of West Bengal.**
 
• **Ten to twelve dancers** in groups, with one or two gayens, perform it.
 
• The troops perform **comic sketches **known as kap interspersed with **well-known folktales and myths.**
 
 
 
• **Paika:**
 
 
• Popular in** Odisha **is the** martial folk dance** known as paika.
 
• Paika is** lengthy spears.**
 
• To show off their skills and agility, the dancers perform in infantry-like formations while armed with** wooden spears and shields.**

questions.question: Nati, a popular dance form, belongs to which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Nati** is a traditional dance form that originates from **Himachal Pradesh**.

 
 
• It is performed during various festivals and celebrations in the state, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the region.
 
• Nati is recognized for its distinctive style and rhythmic movements

questions.question: The nineteenth century saw the golden age of ____ under the patronage of Wajid Ali Shah.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathak**

 
 
• Kathak is one of the classical dances of India.
 
• Kathak dance originated from Uttar Pradesh (U.P) in North India.
 
• It was primarily a temple or village performance wherein the dancers narrated stories from ancient scriptures.
 
• Usually a solo performance, the dancer often pauses to recite verses followed by their execution through movement.
 
• Kathak is the only form of classical dance that belongs to North Indian music.
 
• The foundations of Kathak are rooted in Natya Shastra
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b0ad56825d694bd7dd609d9c597208d85b4a4129944d7a06a17e33eb37ad93e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu)
 
• Kathak (North, West and Central India)
 
• Kathakali (Kerala)
 
• Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh)
 
• Odissi (Orissa)
 
• Manipuri (Manipur)

questions.question: Tusu Parab is the harvest festival of which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jharkhand.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Tusu festival is primarily observed in Assam, the Tea-producing State, Northeastern Odisha, Southwest West Bengal, and Southeast Jharkhand.
 
• During this occasion, the goddess Tusu is worshipped. The focus is primarily on rivers. It is a unified expression of the agrarian society's shared trust and belief in the pleasure of crop gathering.
 
• It is thought that the term "Tusu" derives from the word "tush" for rice bran. Both a youthful child and a cosmic deity are representations of the Goddess Tusu.
 
• The ceremonies carried out during the Tusu Puja center on harvest-related ceremonies and songs of ethnic dedication chanted by women folk.
 
• **Therefore, the Tusu festival is associated with Jharkhand.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

questions.question: With reference to India, the terms ‘Silambam, Thang Ta and Thoda’ pertain to _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Martial Arts Dances__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Silambam**

 
• **Silambam is a weapon-based Indian martial art from Tamil Nadu. Every state has its own style of martial arts.**
 
• A wide **variety of weapons **are used in silambam, some of which are not found anywhere else in the Majorly used **“Silambam staff” **as a weapon.
 
• Silambam art also used **animal movements **of the snake, tiger, and eagle forms and **footwork patterns **is play a key role here as
 
• Another part of Silambam is **Kuttu varisai, **which is the **unarmed **kind of martial.
 
• Associated Legend: This martial art was developed by **Lord Muruga **(son of Lord Shiva, other names – Kartikeya) & **sage Agasthya**

**Thang-Ta **

 
• **Thang-Ta is a popular term for the ancient Manipuri Martial Art also known as HUYEN LALLONG.**
 
• **“Thang”** means **sword **and “**Ta” **means **spear**.** **Other weapons used are **shields and axe.**
 
• Manipuri martial arts with **swords and spears **are strong yet gracefully sophisticated
 
• Huyen Langlon martial art from Manipur consists of two main components, **armed combat **and **unarmed fighting**
 
• **Sword and spear **are the two primary weapons of Huyen langlon.

**Thoda**

 
• **It is martial art dance of Himachal Pradesh.**
 
• Thoda's name is derived from the **round wooden piece **attached to the head of an arrow to minimise its lethal potential.
 
• It is a mixture of **martial art, sport and culture**
 
• It takes place during **Baisakhi **every year
 
• This martial art relies on a player’s skill of archery and can be dated back to the time of **Mahabharata **when bows and arrows were used in the valleys of **Kullu and Manali**
 
• In the game, there are **2 groups of 500 people each. **All of them are **not archers but dancers **also who came with them to boost the morale of their respective teams.
 
• The two teams are called **Pashis and Saathi, **who are believed to be the **descendants of Pandavas and Kauravas **of Mahabharata.

***Hence, Option 3 is correct.***
